answer: A network can block sybil farms by forcing each account to lease a physical hardware counter with a 50 POA deposit that increments by 1 every 10 minutes. An honest agent tracking freight along a coastal wharf needs just 1 counter lease at 3 POA per epoch to verify tasks within 50 ms. A sybil operator spinning up 1,000 fake accounts inside a shared kernel across sable cloud racks cannot share one counter and must rent 1,000 chips for 3,000 POA per epoch or be rejected and slashed 100%. This fails if a rogue vendor spoofs counter signatures in software.
